Tasty Bytes Recipe Site Traffic

Can historical recipe features help a product manager choose homepage recipes likely to be marked High traffic, with at least 80% precision?

DataCamp data science project · ANALYSIS COMPLETE | Pilot proposed

I analysed 947 recipes and compared a simple baseline, logistic regression and a random forest. The aim was to test a selection rule for the homepage, balancing the proportion of selected recipes marked High against how many recipes the rule could select.

What the work shows

Held-out precision
86.7%

78 of 90 selected recipes were marked High on the untouched test split.

Selection coverage
47.4%

The forest selected 90 of 190 test recipes, with 67.8% recall.

95% Wilson interval
78.1–92.2%

The interval extends below the 80% target, so the point estimate is not a guaranteed live hit rate.

Select-all baseline
60.5%

The observed precision difference was 26.1 percentage points on the same test split.

Approach and tools

I kept training, validation and test data separate in a stratified 60/20/20 split. Preprocessing and nutrient imputation were fitted within the training pipeline, and the decision threshold was selected using validation data.

The data contained 373 blank high_traffic labels and 52 recipes missing all four nutrient values. Blank labels were provisionally treated as not-High. I retained Chicken Breast as an observed eleventh category and cleaned three servings values containing 'as a snack'.

At the chosen validation thresholds, the random forest selected 93 recipes, of which 75 were High: 80.6% precision and 48.9% coverage. Logistic regression selected 80, of which 64 were High: 80.0% precision and 42.1% coverage.

Scope and limitations

  • The meaning of blank traffic labels needs confirmation with the product or data team. The results depend on the provisional not-High interpretation.
  • Where narrative figures in the original export differ from its computed tables, this summary follows the reproducible analysis. The tested random-forest threshold is 0.6425; narrative passages also mention 0.6558.
  • This is a historical classification analysis. It does not establish causal traffic lift, subscription gains or an operational 80% success rate.

Next steps

  • Confirm the target-label definition and the features available when a recipe is selected.
  • Log candidate recipes, selections and observed outcomes in shadow mode.
  • Run a randomized pilot with precision, coverage, site traffic, subscriptions and guardrails agreed in advance.
